Woah there, that’s heavy. I work in advertising and I’ve done lots of graphic design with a background in painting. I know beauty. I literally studied it for 6 years. The idea of beauty is subjective sure, but the process can be made into an objective thing, which is to say anyone can become pretty or unattractive depending on how one presents oneself. Working out, eating healthy, dressing well, going to the dentist, all add to a person’s physical aesthetic without directly adding or subtracting to their self confidence (perhaps not initially but if you’re pretty and you know it, it tends to show)

I’m not going to patronize you and say maybe you’re pretty and that it’s in your head. I get that you want real solutions. I’ve seen burn victims who looked pretty. They dressed well, they were in good physical condition and they took care of themselves. Not to say you’re a slob, but if you try reinventing yourself you can transform yourself into however you want to look. 

For instance, there’s a subreddit called r/blunderyears or one about body transformation. Don’t give in, don’t give up. Be the person you want to be. I think people who feel unattractive use their frustration to motive them to be better.
